about: Quiet celebrations (docs/engine.md, "Quiet celebrations"; P11.2): for a date, each enrollment's return after a gap, the books it finished and its finishing, in the order the enrollments were started, then whether the week's reading days were kept. The plans are invented.

cases.name: nothing marked: nothing to celebrate
a first reading is a beginning, not a return
returning: read on Monday, not Tuesday to Thursday, and again on Friday
one reading day not read is simply a day: no return
rest days are not a gap: Friday, then Monday
returning on a rest day: the gap is counted in reading days
a skip is not a reading: no return
a reading logged for an earlier day belongs to that day: nothing today
a reading logged for an earlier day belongs to that day: the return is Thursday's
answering the welcome and then reading is a return
answering the welcome is not reading: the reader who answered yesterday returns today
paused days are not reading days: no gap, and the week's two reading days were read
resuming starts afresh: the reading days before the pause are not a gap
a reading on a paused day is no return
an undone reading is not read: nothing to celebrate
calendar: returning after a gap
finishing a book: Ruth's last chapter read
a part-read chapter leaves the book unfinished
the part-read chapter read later finishes the book that day, and the week is kept
a book finished before today is not finished again; every reading day read keeps the week
a skipped chapter leaves the book unfinished
one reading finishes two books, given in the scheme's order
a second plan through the same book celebrates it again
a book finished by a reading logged for an earlier day belongs to that day
two readings on one day finish the book once
finishing a plan: its last reading read; a finished plan asks nothing more this week
finishing a plan by skipping its last reading
a plan finished before today: reading it again is no return and no second finish, but the book it completes is
calendar: finishing a book, and never the plan; the first week counts from the start
a rhythm is kept only on the week's last reading day
a reading day not read: the week is not kept, and nothing is said of it; Ruth is finished
reading days 1, 3 and 5: the rest days between are not asked about
a week with one reading day says nothing
the first week counts from the start
a paused day is not asked about
two plans: Saturday is a reading day of the second, so Friday keeps nothing yet
two plans: a reading day of either is a reading day, and the week ends on Sunday
an ended enrollment has no celebrations, and its days are not asked about
two plans: each one's celebrations in the order they were started
the example: on Friday the reader has returned and finished Ruth
the example: on Thursday Jonah and the plan are finished, and the week is kept
